title: Go: Observable Stream
description: Build a reactive observable stream library in Go using channels for async data flow with composable operators.

steps.title: Observable with channel
steps.description: Implement an `Observable` struct backed by a `chan interface{}`. Provide `Subscribe()` that returns a receive-only channel, and `Unsubscribe(ch)` to close it. Create a simple observable that emits 5 integers, subscribe, and print each received value.
hints: Observable stores `subscribers map[chan interface{}]struct{}` and a `sync.RWMutex`
`Subscribe()` creates `make(chan interface{}, buffer)` and stores it
Emitting sends to all subscriber channels in a goroutine to avoid blocking

verification.successMessage: Observable correctly emits values to subscriber channels!
verification.failureMessage: Print each received value as 'Received: <value>' from the subscriber.

steps.title: Factory methods: Of, From, Interval
steps.description: Implement `Of(values ...interface{}) *Observable` that emits each argument, `From(slice []interface{}) *Observable` that emits slice elements, and `Interval(d time.Duration) *Observable` that emits incrementing integers on a ticker. Test each factory and print the emitted values.
hints: `Of` launches a goroutine that sends each value and closes the internal subject
`From` is similar but iterates over a slice
`Interval` uses `time.NewTicker` and sends incrementing integers until unsubscribed

verification.successMessage: Factory methods correctly create observables from values, slices, and timers!

steps.title: Map and Filter operators via channels
steps.description: Implement `Map(fn func(interface{}) interface{}) *Observable` that creates a new observable transforming each value through a channel. Implement `Filter(pred func(interface{}) bool) *Observable` similarly. Chain `Of(1,2,3,4,5).Map(x2).Filter(even)` and print the result.
hints: Operators create a new Observable with a goroutine that reads from source, transforms, and writes to output
Map creates a new output channel, reads from source, applies fn, sends to output
Filter reads from source, checks pred, only sends to output if true

verification.successMessage: Map and Filter operators chain correctly to transform async streams!
verification.failureMessage: Print the result of Map(x2).Filter(even) — should only show even doubled values.

steps.title: Merge operator
steps.description: Implement a `Merge(observables ...*Observable) *Observable` that combines multiple observables into a single stream. Values from any source observable are forwarded to the merged output. Create two interval observables at different speeds, merge them, and print the interleaved values.
hints: Merge launches one goroutine per source observable that forwards all values to a shared output channel
Use a `sync.WaitGroup` to track when all source observables complete
Print which source each value came from: `fmt.Printf("[%s] %v\n", sourceID, val)`

verification.successMessage: Merge operator combines multiple observable streams into one interleaved stream!
verification.failureMessage: Print values with their source label, showing interleaved output from both sources.

steps.title: Debounce with time.Ticker
steps.description: Implement a `Debounce(d time.Duration) *Observable` operator that emits a value only after a specified silence period. Use a `time.Timer` that resets on each new value. Test by emitting values in rapid succession (every 50ms for 5 values) with a 200ms debounce and show only the last value is emitted.
hints: Each incoming value resets the timer: `timer.Reset(d)`
Only when the timer fires (no new values arrived) is the latest value forwarded
Use `time.NewTimer(d)` and a select between the source channel and timer channel

verification.successMessage: Debounce operator correctly suppresses rapid values and emits only after silence!
verification.failureMessage: Print 'debounced: <value>' showing only 1 value emitted from 5 rapid inputs.
